correctness.rationale: Four rounds recover the two atom axes and then singleton or transpose-orbit cells. For equal side lengths, matching comparison degrees between axis cells and transitivity canonically align the two axes, with opposite coordinate assignments inside each off-diagonal cell; cellwise order counts force every coordinatewise comparison. Unequal sides yield discrete colours, so competitors need no order axioms. Each four-round colour is definable by a C2 unary formula of rank at most four; one counting layer plus an outer universal quantifier bounds characteristic-sentence rank by six. Standalone checkers verify 113 finite rectangles and exhaust all 512 side-four equitable matching choices, but the infinite claim rests on this explicit proof. For square sides at most three, all matching choices along the two-edge orbit-class path give isomorphic arbitrary binary structures. For every side at least four, crossing only the T2-to-T4 matching yields a nontransitive C2 twin, establishing sharpness of the ambient-class boundary. An independently coded crossed-matching checker confirms nontransitive C2 companions for square sides four through eight.

value.rationale: A natural unbounded family of finite distributive lattices has uniformly bounded C2 description depth. The square case requires nontrivial reconstruction of orbit-size-two comparability matchings, distinguishing orbit-exact refinement from mere discrete refinement. The result gives an exact all-size structural family in finite poset identification with explicitly stated category boundary, independent of any partial enumeration. It also yields the sharp unrestricted-binary-relations threshold: precisely square grids of side at least four admit nonisomorphic C2 twins.
